name: Honey (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Honey [Confectioneries] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: Mato et al. 1998, Enzymatic Determination of Total D-Gluconic Acid in Honey, J. Agric. Food Chem. doi:10.1021/jf970012c
Jasicka-Misiak et al. 2024, Organic Acids in Monofloral and Honeydew Honeys from Poland, PMC12608658
Chen et al. 2024, Free Amino Acid Composition of Seven Honey Species in China, PMC11011401
Stinson et al. 1960, The composition of honey V: organic acids, Arch. Biochem. Biophys. doi:10.1016/0003-9861(60)90003-5
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources are D-fructose (40.9 g/100g) and D-glucose (35.7 g/100g); the defining and previously-missing organic acid is gluconic acid (~0.74 g/100g, from bee glucose oxidase acting on glucose), the principal acid of honey. Free amino acids are dominated by proline. Very low water activity (~17% moisture) means honey is an extreme high-osmolarity sugar medium.
curation_added: gluconic acid (0.74 g/100g — the DOMINANT organic acid of honey, previously absent)
specific sugar amounts (fructose 40.9, glucose 35.7, galactose 3.1, maltose 1.4, sucrose 0.9 g/100g)
minor organic acids with amounts (formic, lactic, quinic, malic, oxalic, citric, succinic, fumaric)
quantified L-proline (dominant free amino acid) + total protein
quantified vitamins and minerals from USDA panel

curation_removed.name: Lactose C12H22O11
curation_removed.reason: Milk disaccharide; biologically implausible in honey (no lactose in nectar/honey). FooDB artifact — remove.

curation_removed.name: Fe2+ mitochondria
curation_removed.reason: BiGG compartmentalized-iron artifact, not a distinct honey nutrient; consolidated into the single measured iron value.

curation_removed.name: Iron (Fe3+)
curation_removed.reason: Duplicate iron entry (redox/compartment variant); consolidated into one iron value.

curation_removed.name: CO2 CO2
curation_removed.reason: Atmospheric/dissolved gas, not a compositional honey nutrient; environmental boundary metabolite.

curation_removed.name: O2 O2
curation_removed.reason: Atmospheric gas, not a honey nutrient; environmental boundary metabolite.

curation_removed.name: Phytomenadione
curation_removed.reason: Vitamin K1 is a plant-leaf phylloquinone; not reported in USDA honey panel and implausible at nutritive level in honey — likely FooDB predicted, drop.

curation_removed.name: L-cystine
curation_removed.reason: Not a characteristic honey free amino acid; sulfur-AA cystine is a likely FooDB prediction artifact, drop unless quantified.

curation_removed.name: Glycine betaine
curation_removed.reason: Not an established quantified honey nutrient; FooDB predicted phytochemical — drop from the growth-relevant profile.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
